note: Independently re-judged against committed source 71b1f3d799; the unrelated working-tree NSSA wire-capture rewrite was excluded. RFC 3101 Section 2.4: "NSSA border routers must originate an LSA for the default destination into all their directly attached NSSAs in order to support intra-AS routing and inter-AS routing." The next sentence permits either Type-3 or Type-7 as Section 2.7 specifies. TestOSPFNSSABorderRouterDefaultsEveryArea configures a backbone and two NSSAs without default-originate and requires the regular NSSA self Type-7 at the zero default LSID; TestOSPFNSSANoSummaryDefaultInjection and TestOSPFNSSAType3SummaryImport independently require the no-summary NSSA Type-3 default, including the actual LSDB lookup/decoded metric in the former. TestOSPFv3NSSABorderRouterOriginatesDefault requires the 0x2007 NSSA-LSA and a zero-length default prefix on the shared reconciler path. applyNSSADefaults derives ABR/attachment from live areas and iterates attached configured NSSAs; wantsType7Default requires a regular NSSA default for an ABR without an operator gate, then uses OriginateNSSA or v6OriginateNSSALSA for the family. OriginateSummaries iterates destination areas and applyAreaTypePolicy injects the Type-3 default for a no-summary NSSA. Removing either default-producing branch makes its positive LSDB assertion fail. TestOSPFNSSAInternalRouterOriginatesNoBorderDefault supplies the clean non-ABR applicability control. The auxiliary v3 internal-router negative also lacks a usable forwarding address and is therefore confounded by Section 2.4 forwarding-address policy; it is not credited as an independent discriminator for this row. The committed checkNSSADefault still configures Ze as the backbone-attached NSSA border router without default-originate, waits for Full and requires FRR to install 0.0.0.0/0 through that border router. Its strengthened requireRouteInstalledVia assertion now requires the exact selected, installed OSPF default entry and the matching active FIB next hop in the same entry, using fields produced by FRR vty_show_ip_route and nexthop_json_helper. The ancillary FRR external-database assertion is not credited as wire-level proof that no Type-5 was flooded, which is a different requirement. The default-origination row remains enforced by the positive default LSAs, clean applicability control and installed-default interop assertion. This is a source rejudgment, with no new runtime or mutation result claimed.
